ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Arabic word means "I"? (1 mark)
   A. مَا اسْمُكَ؟
   B. شُكْرًا
   C. مَرْحَبًا
   D. أَنَا

2. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My name is Ahmad.
   B. I am a pupil (girl).
   C. I am from Kenya.
   D. I am a pupil (boy).

3. What does the small word min mean in anaa min Kiiniya? (1 mark)
   A. for
   B. from
   C. in
   D. with

4. What does the Arabic word أُخْتٌ (ukht) mean? (1 mark)
   A. sister
   B. family
   C. father
   D. grandmother

5. What does the Arabic sentence هَذَا أَبِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have a brother and a sister.
   B. This is my father.
   C. My father works.
   D. This is my mother.

6. Which Arabic sentence means "This is my house." (1 mark)
   A. الْقِطَّةُ تَحْتَ السَّرِيرِ
   B. هَذَا بَيْتِي
   C. الْكِتَابُ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ
   D. الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ

7. Which is a good way of caring for household items? (1 mark)
   A. Leave a lamp near water
   B. Wash cups and plates after use
   C. Throw books on the floor
   D. Leave a knife within reach of small children

8. How is the Arabic word عِنْدَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bijaanibi
   B. ʿinda
   C. taHta
   D. ʿalaa

9. What does the Arabic word الْأَرْبِعَاءُ (al-arbiʿaa') mean? (1 mark)
   A. Wednesday
   B. week
   C. Tuesday
   D. Friday

10. Which polite word means 'excuse me' when you want to speak? (1 mark)
   A. naʿam
   B. ʿafwan
   C. laa
   D. shukran

11. In the sentence fii s-sabaah aakulu khubzan wa bayDan, which words show that the meal is in the morning? (1 mark)
   A. aakulu
   B. wa bayDan
   C. fii s-sabaah
   D. khubzan

12. What does the Arabic sentence أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like juice.
   B. I drink water.
   C. I eat bread.
   D. I like bananas.

13. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ يَدِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I hear with my ear.
   B. I see with my eye.
   C. This is my hand.
   D. I smell with my nose.

14. What does the Arabic sentence أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I smell with my nose.
   B. I hear with my ear.
   C. I see with my eye.
   D. I speak with my mouth.

15. Which sentence says 'I hear with my ear'? (1 mark)
   A. ashummu bi-anfii
   B. araa biʿaynii
   C. aktubu bi-yadii
   D. asmaʿu bi-udhunii

16. Which Arabic sentence means "The weather is cold." (1 mark)
   A. الْجَوُّ غَائِمٌ
   B. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
   C. الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ
   D. الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ

17. What does the Arabic sentence الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is hot.
   B. The weather is cold.
   C. The weather is rainy.
   D. The weather is cloudy.

18. What is the name of the Arabic letter ل? (1 mark)
   A. laam
   B. faa
   C. Daad
   D. yaa

19. How do you read the syllable سَ? (1 mark)
   A. sa
   B. na
   C. li
   D. mi

20. What is the name of the Arabic letter ش? (1 mark)
   A. shiin
   B. Haa
   C. ghayn
   D. thaa

21. How is the Arabic word أَخٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. akh
   B. khaal
   C. usra
   D. ʿamma

22. How do you read the syllable جَ? (1 mark)
   A. nu
   B. ja
   C. muu
   D. li

23. Which question word means 'who'? (1 mark)
   A. kam
   B. man
   C. limaadhaa
   D. ayna

24. What is a prediction? (1 mark)
   A. A copy of a picture
   B. A sensible guess about what will happen next
   C. A spelling test
   D. A list of words

25. What does the Arabic sentence الْأَصْدِقَاءُ فِي الْحَفْلَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. On the table there is a cake.
   B. The friends are at the party.
   C. This is a party.
   D. Above the table there is a balloon.

26. Which Arabic sentence means "I like food." (1 mark)
   A. أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ
   B. الْمَاءُ مُفِيدٌ
   C. السَّمَكُ لَذِيذٌ
   D. الْعَصِيرُ بَارِدٌ

27. What does the Arabic sentence مَا أَجْمَلَ الْبِيئَةَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. And the rain is from the sky.
   B. How beautiful the environment is!
   C. The sun is in the sky.
   D. We dance.

28. What does the Arabic word كُوبٌ (kuub) mean? (1 mark)
   A. knife
   B. cup
   C. cat
   D. cupboard

29. How is the Arabic word بَابٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. saaʿa
   B. kitaab
   C. taawila
   D. baab

30. What does at-taawilatu Sagiira mean? (1 mark)
   A. The chair is new.
   B. The door is clean.
   C. The table is big.
   D. The table is small.

31. How is the Arabic word حَقِيبَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bayt
   B. miftaah
   C. hammaam
   D. haqiiba

32. Which Arabic word means "congratulations"? (1 mark)
   A. رَقْصٌ
   B. مَبْرُوكٌ
   C. حَلْوَى
   D. عِيدٌ

33. What does the Arabic word سُكَّرٌ (sukkar) mean? (1 mark)
   A. bread
   B. milk
   C. carrots
   D. sugar

34. What does the Arabic word لِسَانٌ (lisaan) mean? (1 mark)
   A. ear
   B. tongue
   C. finger
   D. body

35. Which Arabic word means "leg"? (1 mark)
   A. بَطْنٌ
   B. رِجْلٌ
   C. سِنٌّ
   D. ظَهْرٌ

36. What does al-jawwu mumtir mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is cold.
   B. The weather is sunny.
   C. The weather is rainy.
   D. The weather is cloudy.

37. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ شَمْسٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is hot.
   B. This is the sun.
   C. This is rain.
   D. The wind is strong.

38. What does the Arabic word بِيئَةٌ (bii'a) mean? (1 mark)
   A. tree
   B. sun
   C. sky
   D. environment

39. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ غُرْفَتِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my room.
   B. In the kitchen there is a table.
   C. In the room there is a bed.
   D. I like my house.

40. Which Arabic sentence means "I like my house." (1 mark)
   A. فِي الْغُرْفَةِ سَرِيرٌ
   B. أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي
   C. هَذِهِ غُرْفَتِي
   D. فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write four weather features in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

42. Translate into English: unadhdhifu asnaanii (2 marks)

43. Say what the words abii yaʿmalu and ummii tatbukhu mean, and name one thing each parent does. (4 marks) (4 marks)

44. Translate into English: alʿabu yawma s-sabt (2 marks)

45. Translate into English: hal tuhibbu l-mawz? (2 marks)

46. Write an Arabic question and its answer that you could use to find out who a woman in a photograph is. Use English letters. (3 marks) (3 marks)

47. Translate into English: al-asdiqaa'u fii l-hafla. (2 marks) (2 marks)

48. Explain what pace is and describe a good pace for reading aloud. (3 marks) (3 marks)

49. Read these words and write their sounds in English letters with meanings: مَرْحَبًا and شُكْرًا. (4 marks) (4 marks)

50. Complete the word شُكْ_ا with the missing letter and give its meaning. (2 marks) (2 marks)

51. Explain how the weather affects our daily life. Give two examples. (3 marks) (3 marks)

52. Translate into English: maa ismuki? (2 marks)

53. Translate into English: haadhaa matar (2 marks)

54. Describe how a group can stage a poem at an interclass festival. (4 marks) (4 marks)

55. Write five weather or environment words in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

56. Say why food is important for human life and name two foods grown in Kenya. (3 marks) (3 marks)

57. Explain how to build a vocabulary bank for the theme of the body. (3 marks) (3 marks)

58. List the six Arabic letters that do not join to the letter that follows them. (3 marks) (3 marks)

59. Translate into English: fii l-matbakhi taawila wa kursii. (2 marks) (2 marks)

60. Give three differences between the Arabic and the English alphabets. (3 marks) (3 marks)

61. Translate into English: al-qalamu fii l-haqiiba (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — أَنَا
   أَنَا (anaa) means I.

2. D — I am a pupil (boy).
   أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ (anaa tilmiidh) means: I am a pupil (boy).

3. B — from
   min means 'from', so the sentence says 'I am from Kenya'.

4. A — sister
   أُخْتٌ (ukht) means sister.

5. B — This is my father.
   هَذَا أَبِي (haadhaa abii) means: This is my father.

6. B — هَذَا بَيْتِي
   هَذَا بَيْتِي (haadhaa baytii) means: This is my house.

7. B — Wash cups and plates after use
   Cleaning items after use helps them to last and keeps the home safe.

8. B — ʿinda
   عِنْدَ is read ʿinda and means at (near, by).

9. A — Wednesday
   الْأَرْبِعَاءُ (al-arbiʿaa') means Wednesday.

10. B — ʿafwan
   ʿafwan is used to say 'excuse me' or 'pardon' before speaking.

11. C — fii s-sabaah
   sabaah means morning, so fii s-sabaah is 'in the morning'.

12. B — I drink water.
   أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ (ashrabu l-maa'a) means: I drink water.

13. C — This is my hand.
   هَذِهِ يَدِي (haadhihi yadii) means: This is my hand.

14. B — I hear with my ear.
   أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي (asmaʿu bi-udhunii) means: I hear with my ear.

15. D — asmaʿu bi-udhunii
   asmaʿu means I hear and udhun means ear.

16. B — الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
   الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ (al-jawwu baarid) means: The weather is cold.

17. A — The weather is hot.
   الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ (al-jawwu haarr) means: The weather is hot.

18. A — laam
   The letter ل is called laam.

19. A — sa
   سَ is read sa.

20. A — shiin
   The letter ش is called shiin.

21. A — akh
   أَخٌ is read akh and means brother.

22. B — ja
   جَ is read ja.

23. B — man
   man means who. ayna means where, kam means how many and limaadhaa means why.

24. B — A sensible guess about what will happen next
   We use clues to predict what may happen next.

25. B — The friends are at the party.
   الْأَصْدِقَاءُ فِي الْحَفْلَةِ (al-asdiqaa'u fii l-hafla) means: The friends are at the party.

26. A — أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ
   أُحِبُّ الطَّعَامَ (uhibbu T-taʿaam) means: I like food.

27. B — How beautiful the environment is!
   مَا أَجْمَلَ الْبِيئَةَ (maa ajmala l-bii'a) means: How beautiful the environment is!

28. B — cup
   كُوبٌ (kuub) means cup.

29. D — baab
   بَابٌ is read baab and means door.

30. D — The table is small.
   taawila is table and Sagiira means small.

31. D — haqiiba
   حَقِيبَةٌ is read haqiiba and means bag.

32. B — مَبْرُوكٌ
   مَبْرُوكٌ (mabruuk) means congratulations.

33. D — sugar
   سُكَّرٌ (sukkar) means sugar.

34. B — tongue
   لِسَانٌ (lisaan) means tongue.

35. B — رِجْلٌ
   رِجْلٌ (rijl) means leg.

36. C — The weather is rainy.
   mumtir means rainy.

37. B — This is the sun.
   هَذِهِ شَمْسٌ (haadhihi shams) means: This is the sun.

38. D — environment
   بِيئَةٌ (bii'a) means environment.

39. A — This is my room.
   هَذِهِ غُرْفَتِي (haadhihi ghurfatii) means: This is my room.

40. B — أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي
   أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي (uhibbu baytii) means: I like my house.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: shams (sun), sahaab (clouds), riih (wind), matar (rain).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: I clean my teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: abii yaʿmalu: My father works. ummii tatbukhu: My mother cooks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each translation and 1 mark for each role named.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: I play on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do you like bananas?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: man haadhihi? haadhihi ummii. (Who is this? This is my mother.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the question, 1 mark for the answer, 1 mark for correct use of haadhihi for a woman.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends are at the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'the friends' and 1 mark for 'at the party'.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pace is the speed of reading. A good pace is steady, not too fast so that listeners understand, and not so slow that the sentence sounds broken.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 2 marks for the description.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: mar-ha-ban (hello) and shuk-ran (thank you).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reading and 1 mark for each meaning.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: شُكْرًا: the missing letter is raa (ر). It means thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the letter and 1 mark for the meaning.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain helps crops to grow; hot sun makes us look for shade; we choose our clothes by the weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the idea and 1 mark for each example.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: What is your name? (to a girl)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is rain.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a group; share the lines and actions; stand facing the audience; say the poem together with actions; bow at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example shams (sun), sahaab (clouds), matar (rain), riih (wind), samaa' (sky).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Food gives energy to grow, learn and stay healthy. Examples are maize and bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the importance and 1 mark each for two foods.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write each new word with its sound and meaning, add a small drawing, and keep the words on cards or a page for practice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: alif, daal, dhaal, raa, zaay and waaw.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six; 2 marks for four or five; 1 mark for two or three.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Arabic is read from right to left; it has no capital letters; letters join and change shape; it uses marks for short vowels; it has sounds like ʿayn and Haa that English does not have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference, up to 3.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The pen is in the bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.
